chunks: And my father narrated to us, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

Who are the Aal of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family)? He said: His offspring. I said: His Household? He said: The Succeeding Imams. I said: Who is his 'Itra? He said: The People of the Cloak. I said: Who is his Ummah? He said: The believers who verified what he brought from Allah, Exalted and Glorious, those adhering to the Two Weighty Things which they were ordered to hold fast to: The Book of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, and his 'Itra, his Household, from whom Allah removed impurity and purified them with a complete purification. And they are the Two Successors over the nation after him (peace be upon him).
ai.seo_question: Who are the Ahl al-Bayt and Itra according to this hadith from Maani al-Akhbar?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq clarifies the hierarchical distinction between the Prophet's lineage ('Aal'), his purified family ('Ahl al-Bayt' identified here as the Imams), and his broader community ('Ummah'). It establishes the 'People of the Cloak' (Ahl al-Kisa) as the core of the 'Itra' and links the definition of the true 'Ummah' to those who hold fast to the Two Weighty Things (al-Thaqalayn), thereby reinforcing the Shia doctrine of the inseparability of the Quran and the Ahl al-Bayt.
